title: Producer Consumer Buffer
goal: A practitioner can visually assess the Producer Consumer Buffer scenario using its published diagram convention.

rubric.must: Places are circles and transitions are bars or rectangles, with arrows only between the two node kinds.
Initial tokens are visibly shown in the resource or state places needed to start the process.
The picture visibly supports the stated process progression through its marked places and transitions.
The net visibly expresses the scenario's buffer, shared resource, semaphore, cycle, or workflow choice control.
Tokens, labels, and arrows remain readable as a one-page Petri net.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the petri exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The drawing visibly represents the complete bounded-buffer Petri net: five circular places, two bar transitions, the required directed arcs, two tokens in Empty, one token each in Ready and Consumer, capacity 2, and the firing sequence Produce → Consume.

items.evidence: Empty, Ready, Item, Consumer, and Done are circles; Produce and Consume are bars. All visible directed arcs connect places to transitions or transitions to places.
Empty visibly contains two tokens, while Ready and Consumer each contain one token, matching the initial marking required to enable production and subsequent consumption.

Ready and Empty feed Produce; Produce returns Ready and creates Item. Item and Consumer feed Consume; Consume returns Consumer and Empty and marks Done. This visibly supports Produce followed by Consume.
The shared bounded-buffer control is visible through the Empty place labeled “empty slots · capacity: 2,” the Item place, and the producer/consumer return cycles.
Tokens, place and transition labels, arrowheads, capacity annotation, and the displayed firing sequence are readable on the one-page diagram.
